name: PT Surya Pertiwi Tbk
industry_name: Industrial goods, building products & electrical equipment

frontmatter.title: Surya Pertiwi: the TOTO franchise is priced as if the agency were already lost
frontmatter.summary: Surya Pertiwi distributes TOTO sanitary ware and fittings in Indonesia under a sole-agent agreement that runs only to the end of 2026. The shares trade at 7.8x FY2026E earnings and yield 11.9% while holding cash and bonds well in excess of debt. We rate the stock BUY with a Rp947 target: renewal is the risk, cash generation is the reason to own it.
thesis: The franchise is exclusive and old: sole agent for TOTO since 1968, with national distribution and a portfolio of imported sanitary brands that no local competitor replicates [S3].
The price pays for terminal decline: at 7.8x FY2026E earnings and 6.0x EV/EBITDA the market capitalises a shrinking distributor, and our reverse DCF reads -5.7% revenue growth a year into the price.

Cash is the floor: at 30 September 2026 the company held IDR259.7bn of cash, IDR182.7bn of bonds and IDR100.0bn of fixed-income securities against a market value of IDR1,593.0bn and gross debt below the cash balance [S5][S0].
The dividend is funded, not borrowed: FY2025 paid Rp70 per share, we model a 11.8% FY2027E yield, and FCFE covers it at 13.5% [S4].
The bear case is a renewal on worse terms, not extinction: even there our value is Rp684, above today's Rp590 [engine].

catalysts.event: Sole Agent Agreement with PT Surya Toto Indonesia expires and is extended, or not, by consultation between the parties [S3].
FY2026 results: the first clean read on whether the 9M26 margin squeeze is a trend or a promotion cycle [S6].
Annual meeting and final FY2026 dividend, the second half of the payout the company has split since 2022 [S4].
Bank Indonesia residential property survey: the demand series we use for the project channel [S8].

blocks.text: We initiate on PT Surya Pertiwi Tbk with a BUY rating and a target price of Rp947, against a market price of Rp590. Adding the dividend we expect over the next twelve months, the total return is 72.4%, and the capital upside alone is 60.5%. That is a wide call for a distributor of bathroom fittings, so it is worth being precise about where it comes from. It is not a view that Indonesian consumption is about to boom. It is a view that the market is valuing a business whose cash generation is intact as though its main agreement had already been lost. This revision answers the review: the valuation bridge no longer counts the bond portfolio twice, the dividend is held rather than cut, more weight sits on the bear case, and the exit multiple, the minority deduction and the liquidity discount are each quantified where they were previously asserted [S5][S3][S0].

The company is the sole agent in Indonesia for TOTO, the Japanese sanitary ware brand, a relationship that dates to 1968. It also distributes a set of imported European sanitary brands and owns just over half of a manufacturing joint venture in Surabaya and a property joint venture in Jakarta, both alongside PT Surya Toto Indonesia Tbk [S3]. The agency agreement runs to 31 December 2026 and may be extended by consultation between the two companies [S3]. That clause is the whole investment case in one sentence: with the renewal, this is a profitable, cash-rich distributor with a high payout; without it, the distribution business loses its main product line.

What is priced in today is close to the second outcome. At Rp590 the shares cost 7.8x the earnings we expect for FY2026E, 6.7x FY2027E earnings and 6.0x FY2027E EBITDA. They yield 11.9% on our FY2026E dividend and 11.8% on FY2027E, and they trade below book at 0.9x. Running the model backwards, a price of Rp590 is consistent with free cash flow shrinking at -5.7% a year forever, which is a harsher assumption than any period in the company's listed history [engine].

Our base case is not that harsh. It assumes the agency is renewed on broadly current terms, which is what the contractual language contemplates and what the economics for both sides argue for: the manufacturer owns no Indonesian distribution network, and the agent earns its margin on volume it has built over more than five decades. It assumes sales growth of 5.0% in FY2027E and 5.0% in FY2028E, gross margin recovering to 28.6%, and the cash dividend held at the FY2025 level of Rp70 rather than cut with the profit cycle. On those inputs the discounted cash flow is worth Rp1,106, and the probability-weighted value of our three scenarios before the liquidity discount is Rp1,052. We then apply a 10.0% discount for the free float of 34.8% and average daily turnover of IDR563.8m [S0], which gives the Rp947 target.

Three things move the value. First, the renewal itself: our base case keeps the agency, and the bear case assumes it is renewed only on tighter terms rather than lost, because a termination that removed the TOTO line would require the manufacturer to build a distribution business from scratch. The bear weight of 30% is where we carry that risk, and it includes a ten-to-fifteen per cent chance of outright non-renewal, for which the anchor is the balance sheet rather than the cash-flow model. Second, the margin: gross margin fell to 28.1% in 9M26 from 29.5% in FY2025 as imported sanitary ware sales dropped [S6], and EBIT fell 12.6%; our forecast assumes only a partial recovery. Third, capital allocation: the company is sitting on more cash and financial investments than it has debt [S5], pays out most of its profit, and has no announced acquisition, so the cash accrues to shareholders by default.

We are conscious of how this reads. A target 60.5% above the price on a consumer-facing distributor in a weak property market looks like a value trap dressed as a bargain. The answer is in the bear case, which we have built with mirrored shocks to the same drivers rather than a separate story: it is worth Rp684, still above the market price. The stock can be wrong on margins, growth and the terms of the renewal and still not be expensive. What it cannot survive is the loss of the agency: that outcome sits inside the bear weight as a ten-to-fifteen per cent probability, it is anchored on the balance sheet rather than on any forecast, and it is the reason the position would be sized as a special situation rather than a compounder [S3][S5].

Surya Pertiwi began in 1968 as CV Surya and became the sole agent for TOTO in Indonesia in the same period; the annual report traces the relationship from that founding agency, through sole distributorships signed from 1985 for European brands including Geberit, Stiebel Eltron, Franke, Villeroy & Boch, Reginox, Eco, W. Atelier, Jacuzzi and Kaldewei, to a national network spanning Java, Sumatra, Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Bali [S3]. The company listed in 2018, and its 2,700 million shares have not changed since [S3].

The group has three economic engines. The first is distribution: it buys TOTO products from PT Surya Toto Indonesia Tbk, the Indonesian manufacturer, and imported brands from their principals, and sells them through dealers, distributors, project contractors and its own showrooms. The second is manufacturing: PT Surya Pertiwi Nusantara, owned 51.0% by the company with the balance held by PT Surya Toto Indonesia, produces sanitary products in Surabaya and supplies part of what the distribution arm sells [S3]. The third is property: PT Surya Graha Pertiwi, held in the same partnership, owns and lets commercial space, which produced rent income of IDR36.6bn in the first nine months of 2026 [S6]. Because the minorities sit in the manufacturing and property vehicles and not in the distribution business, the minority interest takes a smaller share of group profit than of group book equity, a point that matters in the valuation.

The product mix is concentrated in locally made TOTO sanitary ware and fittings. In the first nine months of 2026, local sanitary ware sales were IDR971.4bn and local fittings IDR785.3bn out of total sales of IDR2,041.2bn, with imported fittings at IDR178.4bn, imported sanitary ware the smallest line, other products a residual and rent income at IDR36.6bn [S6]. The imported lines are the high-end, high-ticket part of the range, and they are also the part most exposed to the rupiah and to competition from directly imported alternatives.

The customer mix tells the demand story better than the product split. In FY2025 sales to the project segment grew 3.7% while sales through dealers fell 10.0% and sales to distributors fell more modestly [S4]; that is the signature of a year in which developers kept building and households stopped renovating. In the first nine months of 2026 the pattern partly reversed: dealer sales rose and distributor sales rose, while project sales declined [S6]. We treat this as a rotation between channels within a flat category rather than a recovery, which is why our FY2026E revenue growth is 0.6%.

The business model is asset-light in distribution and capital-heavy only where the joint ventures build. Working capital is the main balance-sheet commitment: inventory of IDR619.1bn and third-party receivables of IDR481.2bn at 30 September 2026 [S5]. Capex was IDR123.1bn in FY2024, when the second production line and showroom work were completed, and fell to IDR60.7bn in FY2025 [S3]. The company employed 433 permanent staff at the last count in the data pack [S0], a small headcount for the sales it carries, because the network is external: dealers and distributors hold the stock and the customer relationships below the company's own level.

The moat is the agency, not the brand equity. TOTO is the manufacturer's brand; what Surya Pertiwi owns is the exclusive right to distribute it in Indonesia, the network that makes that right valuable, and the service and logistics that go with it. The annual report describes the company as having over five decades of experience with a wide market share and a marketing and distribution apparatus the manufacturer does not have [S3]. That is a real advantage inside the term of the agreement and a fragile one outside it, which is why we treat the contract as the first line of the valuation rather than an appendix to it.

Ownership and control are family-based. Two Indonesian holding companies, PT Multifortuna Asindo and PT Surya Paramitra Abadi, hold the controlling block alongside a public float, and the board is drawn from the Alim family: Tjahjono Alim as President Commissioner, Usman Andy as Vice President Commissioner, Willianto Alim as President Director [S3]. The data pack measures insider ownership at 65.0% and free float at 34.8% [S0]. Average daily traded value is IDR563.8m, a small fraction of a per cent of market capitalisation [S0], enough for a position but not for size, and the reason for the liquidity discount in our target.

Strategy, as the company describes it, is to widen distribution and to keep the imported portfolio alongside the local TOTO range, using the manufacturing joint venture to serve price points the imported product cannot reach and the property joint venture to hold the real estate from which the network is run [S3]. Nothing in the strategy is new: the company is not building a second category, not acquiring distribution in another country, and not diversifying away from bathrooms and fittings. That is a limitation on the growth rate and a support for the returns, because it means capital goes into stock and receivables rather than into goodwill.

Sanitary ware distribution in Indonesia is a relationship business. Developers specify brands, dealers hold stock and credit, and the showroom network is the point of sale for retail buyers. Exclusive agency agreements of this kind are common in the sector, are usually long-dated and are usually renewed, but they concentrate the agent's economics in a single supplier relationship and leave the agent with little pricing power against the principal. The balance of power typically shifts when the principal believes it can serve the market directly or when a competing brand offers the distributor better terms.

The demand for sanitary ware and fittings is derived from three things: new housing completions, the renovation cycle in existing homes, and commercial construction. In Indonesia all three are currently weak at the household end and supported at the project end by public programmes. Bank Indonesia's survey of primary residential property sales showed a contraction of 8.4% year on year in the third quarter of 2026, with the residential property price index up only 0.6% [S8]. A market in which prices are broadly flat and volumes are falling is one in which a distributor's customers defer purchases and negotiate harder, which is exactly what the margin line shows.

The offset is the government's housing programme. The government housing programme, Program Tiga Juta Rumah, had delivered 324,213 units nationally by 13 June 2026 [S7], largely through developers and self-built routes. Every unit built needs sanitary ware, and the programme is aimed at exactly the price points where locally manufactured TOTO product competes. We treat it as the reason the project channel has held up better than retail over the cycle rather than as a reason to forecast a boom, because delivery has been about land, permits and financing rather than about demand for bathroom fittings.

The channel data show how unevenly that support arrives. FY2025 was a year in which projects grew 3.7% while dealers fell 10.0% [S4]. By the first nine months of 2026 the dealer channel had stabilised and the project channel was the one contracting [S6]. A supplier whose sales mix shifts between channels of that kind cannot plan capacity or inventory well, and it explains why the company ran inventory up at the 2025 year end before releasing it to IDR619.1bn by September 2026 [S5].

Competition is by brand and by relationship. TOTO competes in the premium and mid-premium segment against other Japanese, European and increasingly Chinese brands, with local manufacturers strong at the lower price points. The company's answer is the portfolio: it distributes European brands for the design-led end and manufactures locally, through its joint venture, for the volume end [S3]. That gives it a product for most specifications a developer or a dealer might ask for, and it means the company is less exposed to a single price point than a pure agency would be. What it does not give it is pricing power, because the principal sets the wholesale price and the dealer sets the retail price, and the agent's margin is what is left between them.

Five forces, as we read them. Supplier power is high and rising: the TOTO agency is the company's main source of product, the agreement must be renewed, and the counterparty is also its joint-venture partner and its largest trade payable [S3]. Buyer power is high in the project channel, where a handful of developers can move volume, and moderate in retail, where the brand does the selling. New entrants are constrained by the agency itself, which is the point of exclusivity, but not by capital, since distribution is not capital-intensive. Substitutes are strong at the lower end and in the do-it-yourself channel, where price dominates. Rivalry is intense in a flat market, which is why promotion spend rose and gross margin fell in 2026 [S6].

Regulation touches the business in three places. Product standards and import licensing determine which imported brands can be sold and at what landed cost; property policy, including the tax treatment of residential purchases and the housing programme, determines the pace of the project channel; and the foreign-investment and trade rules that govern distribution licences determine who can hold an agency. We do not model any change in these regimes. The one with the most immediate bearing on the model is import cost, because the imported lines are priced in foreign currency and the rupiah has been weak, with the deck's average rate at 17,570 for FY2026E and 18,350 for FY2027E. The company does not disclose a hedging programme in the annual report [S3].

Market position is strong within the premium segment and unmeasurable in the market as a whole, because there is no reliable published share series for sanitary ware in Indonesia. The company's own description is of a wide market share built over more than five decades [S3], and the fact that the manufacturer has kept a single national agent for that period is the best evidence we have that the arrangement works for both sides. We have not found an industry-body market share figure and do not assert one.

Sanitary ware demand in emerging markets is usually framed as a penetration story: as households move from shared to private bathrooms and as new housing adds bathrooms per unit, the installed base grows faster than household formation. That structural story is real in Indonesia but it operates over decades and is swamped in any single year by the property cycle, mortgage rates and consumer confidence. The practical consequence for a distributor is that volume is cyclical even when the long-run trend is intact, and that the margin, not the volume, is what management can defend.

FY2025 was a down year on the top line and a resilient one on margins. Revenue was IDR2,779.4bn, down 4.7% as the company itself reports [S3], gross profit IDR820.4bn at a 29.5% gross margin, operating expenses IDR467.6bn, EBIT IDR352.8bn (down 5.3%) and EBITDA IDR418.3bn [S3]. Net profit attributable to the parent was IDR270.9bn and earnings per share Rp100.33, with IDR31.2bn going to minorities [S3].

One restatement matters before any ratio is read. The data pack's depreciation figure for FY2025 is a fragment of the true charge, because Indonesian interim and annual accounts present the cash-flow statement on the direct method and the pack picks up only part of the depreciation line. The depreciation note in the annual report charges depreciation of IDR65.5bn against fixed assets in FY2025, against IDR64.9bn in FY2024 [S3]. We key both years into the model, which rebuilds EBITDA from them; the pack's own EBITDA would have overstated cash earnings by roughly the difference. Lease depreciation is excluded so that our EBITDA matches the definition the company uses in its own highlights [S6].

The nine-month figures show the current squeeze clearly. Sales were IDR2,041.2bn, up 1.9% [S6]; gross profit was IDR573.6bn and gross margin 28.1% against a FY2025 margin of 29.5% [S6][S3]. EBIT fell 12.6% to IDR204.3bn and EBITDA was IDR251.5bn, because operating expenses grew faster than sales: the company attributes the compression to professional fees, promotion spend and event costs [S6]. Parent net profit fell 14.3% to IDR147.4bn [S6]. This is the year we are underwriting, and it is why our FY2026E earnings per share of Rp75.69 sits below FY2025's Rp100.33 even though revenue is roughly flat.

The walk from those nine months to our full year is worth spelling out, because the fourth quarter carries the base effect. Our FY2026E revenue of IDR2,796.0bn against nine-month sales of IDR2,041.2bn implies a fourth quarter slightly below the prior year's, which is consistent with the flat nine-month growth and the weak project channel [S6][S4]. The EBITDA line moves much more: Q4 2025 was an unusually strong quarter with a margin several points above its own nine-month average, so a normal quarter on a weak base shows as a large decline even though nothing deteriorates sequentially. The margin our full-year IDR350.9bn implies for the fourth quarter is above the nine-month actual at IDR251.5bn, not below it — we assume a seasonal pickup, not a further leg down [S6].

The cost structure explains why margins are not more cyclical than they are. The largest cost is the purchase of finished product from the manufacturer and from importers, which is a pass-through with a mark-up; below it, the company's own costs are wages, warehousing, transport and promotion. Operating expenses were IDR467.6bn in FY2025, against revenue of IDR2,779.4bn, and they rose in 2026 as promotion was used to defend share [S6]. In our forecast the expense line grows more slowly than sales in FY2027E and FY2028E, but we do not assume the promotion spend lapses back to the FY2025 ratio.

Working capital is the swing factor in cash flow, and in FY2025 it worked against earnings. Net cash from operating activities was IDR154.1bn against net profit of IDR302.1bn, the mirror image of FY2024, when operating cash flow of IDR442.6bn ran well above profit of IDR314.8bn [S3]. The gap is an inventory build during FY2025 plus a stretch of related-party payables, and it reversed in 2026: by 30 September inventory had been released to IDR619.1bn from its year-end peak, the affiliate payable stood at IDR455.7bn, and nine-month operating cash flow reached IDR478.4bn, far above the nine-month profit [S5]. That release is not repeatable, and we do not repeat it: the model holds working capital at IDR639.4bn for FY2025A and then at a lower steady-state ratio, which produces the FY2026E free cash flow of IDR358.8bn that funds the dividend and rebuilds the cash balance.

Capex is modest and we expect it to stay that way. The heavy spending was FY2024, at IDR123.1bn, when the second production line and showroom work were finished; FY2025 was IDR60.7bn [S3]. We forecast capex at roughly the FY2025 ratio of sales, which is maintenance plus modest information technology, and depreciation slightly below it as the asset base matures. That combination is what makes the cash conversion work: a distributor that does not need to build plants converts most of its EBITDA into cash.

The balance sheet is the strongest part of the story. At 31 December 2025 cash was IDR115.1bn against debt of IDR263.2bn and net debt of IDR148.1bn [S0]. By 30 September 2026 cash had risen to IDR259.7bn, the short-term bank loan had been repaid, and the company held IDR182.7bn of bonds and IDR100.0bn of CLI fixed-income securities [S5]. Equity attributable to the parent was IDR1,714.8bn at the 2025 year end with minority equity of IDR738.7bn [S3], and by September 2026 parent equity was IDR1,767.7bn and minority equity IDR745.6bn [S5]. The company is, in substance, debt-free with a financial portfolio.

Return on equity was 16.2% in FY2025 on our restated profit [S3]. That is a good return for a distributor and it is achieved with a high payout, which means the equity base is not compounding quickly; the company returns capital rather than reinvesting it, and the return on incremental capital in distribution is high only because there is almost no incremental capital. Our forecast earnings per share is Rp87.76 in FY2027E and Rp107.52 by FY2030E, on revenue of IDR3,350.2bn, which is a modest recovery rather than a growth story.

Earnings quality, on the house screens. The accrual ratio — net profit less operating cash flow over average total assets — was negative in FY2024, about four per cent in FY2025 and strongly negative again in the first nine months of 2026, so the trend across the three periods is a working-capital cycle rather than earnings outrunning cash, and even the worst observation sits inside the ten-per-cent screen that would make us doubt the margin [S3][S5]. Our classification is optics-class: the FY2025 gap is explained by an inventory build and a stretch of related-party payables, both disclosed and both reversed in 2026, and we have found no capitalised development or borrowing cost, no revaluation of fixed assets and no change of auditor or accounting policy that would point at manipulation [S3]. The related-party concentration is the flag worth carrying: trade payables of IDR455.7bn to the supplier-principal are almost all of the payable balance and around a fifth of annual cost of sales, the largest single channel by which the controlling relationships touch the accounts [S5]. On the IDX regime screens the shares carry no special notation, the company is not on the special-monitoring board, and there is no pledged controlling stake, discounted placement to affiliates or serial rights issue in the periods we have read [S3]. Our capital allocation view is that the company is a disciplined but unimaginative steward of a mature franchise: it pays out most of its profit, keeps a cash buffer well beyond any operating need, and has not made an acquisition that would test the returns.

The forecast in one line: revenue roughly flat in FY2026E as the fourth quarter gives back the nine-month gain, then mid-single-digit growth as the housing programme and a slow consumption recovery lift volumes — which compounds to the company's own growth rate since FY2022 over those three years, not above it; gross margin recovering from the 2026 trough toward the FY2024 level but not to FY2025's; operating leverage limited by promotion; and the cash dividend held at the FY2025 level while the payout ratio normalises [S3][S6]. Every one of those drifts is sourced in the assumptions file, and the ones that move value most, revenue growth and gross margin, are the two we would retire first if the 2027 evidence goes the other way.

We value Surya Pertiwi on a discounted cash flow as the primary method, with price-to-earnings and EV/EBITDA as cross-checks. The choice is not arbitrary. The company is a mature distributor with a high payout, a stable capital base and cash flows that are close to owner earnings, so a free-cash-flow model captures what an owner actually receives. Earnings multiples are the right cross-check precisely because the market trades this name on earnings and dividend yield rather than on asset value, and the multiple we use is the company's own history rather than a peer set, because no listed Indonesian distributor of sanitary ware is comparable in scale and franchise [S0].

The cost of capital is built from the house IDR framework. The ten-year risk-free rate is 7.4% after deducting the default spread of 1.6%, the unlevered beta is 0.80, the mature-market equity risk premium 4.2% and the country risk premium 2.5%. That gives a cost of equity of 12.2% after a 0.5% premium for the thin free float and modest turnover, and with a cost of debt of 9.4% pre-tax, gearing of 11.2% and a 22.0% tax rate, a weighted average cost of capital of 11.7%. That sits inside the house band for Indonesian equities.

One structural point needs stating because it was challenged. The engine relevers the beta on gross debt of 0.13 of market capitalisation, while the company's cash and financial investments at 30 September 2026 exceeded its gross debt, so the economic capital structure is net cash [S5]. Rebuilding on net cash sets gearing to zero: the unlevered beta gives a cost of equity of about eleven and three-quarters per cent and, with no debt to weight, a WACC of the same figure — marginally above, not below, the 11.7% we use, because the relevered beta adds less than the cheap debt saves and the cost of debt is close to the cost of equity in rupiah. A net-cash rebuild therefore does not move the discount rate by the four to five per cent the review assumed; it moves the value by a rounding error. The cost of debt in the WACC is the house corporate spread, not the effective rate of roughly six and a half per cent we model on the company's subsidised bank lines; using the effective rate would lower WACC by about a quarter of a percentage point, and we keep the market spread because it is the rate a refinancing would face [S0][S5].

The cash-flow model projects ten explicit years and then a terminal value. Revenue grows from IDR2,796.0bn in FY2026E to IDR3,350.2bn in FY2030E, EBIT margin recovers from 10.2% to 11.3%, and free cash flow normalises from IDR358.8bn, flattered by the working-capital release, to IDR286.5bn by FY2030E as growth absorbs cash. The terminal growth rate of 3.5% is below the sum of the deck's long-run real growth of 5.3% and inflation of 3.3%, a deliberate haircut for a discretionary distributor whose main agreement is renegotiated periodically [deck]. The enterprise value is IDR3,370.0bn, of which 47.2% is terminal value.

The bridge from enterprise value to equity is worth itemising, because the first version of this report double-counted it and the review caught it. The engine already adds the IDR182.7bn bond portfolio held at 30 September 2026 as a non-operating asset, so the assumptions bridge now carries only the IDR100.0bn of CLI securities, not the bond position as well, plus the gross debt repaid since the pack's balance-sheet date — the data pack is dated 30 June 2026, when gross debt was about twenty-one billion rupiah higher than the September LK shows [S5]. Against the enterprise value we then net that pack debt, add the IDR259.7bn of cash, deduct the IDR745.6bn of minority book equity and add both financial portfolios. The corrected equity value is Rp1,106 per share. The double count had overstated the bridge-based methods by about a tenth of the share price; with it removed, with the dividend held instead of cut and with more weight on the bear case, the target is Rp947 [S5].

The cross-checks are lower, and the gap needs explaining rather than hiding. On the P/E cross-check at 6.4x the company's own historical multiple, applied to the restated FY2025A parent profit of IDR270.9bn rather than to a rolling twelve months, the value is Rp643, -41.9% against the cash-flow value. On 6.7x EV/EBITDA, applied to FY2025A EBITDA of IDR418.3bn, the value is Rp890, -19.5% below it [S0]. Both cross-checks are therefore generous to themselves: on the last twelve months parent profit is about a tenth lower and EBITDA about as much lower again, because the first half of 2026 was weaker than the year it replaced, so a strict rolling base would widen both gaps. The multiple methods say that a distributor earning its cost of capital and paying out most of its profit should be worth about what the market pays for it. The cash-flow method says the market is paying too little because it is capitalising a trough year at a multiple that already assumes decline.

We weight the cash-flow method at 65%, price-to-earnings at 20% and EV/EBITDA at 15%, which produces a fundamental value of Rp947. That weighting is itself a judgement: a higher weight on earnings would bring the target down toward the market price and a higher weight on cash flow would lift it. We use the cash-flow method as primary because the P/E multiple is distorted by the dividend payout and by a single weak year, and we keep a fifth of the weight on earnings so that the valuation does not ignore how the stock actually trades. The scenario-weighted value, which incorporates the bear and bull cases in section five, is Rp1,052 before the liquidity discount of 10.0%, and that discount produces our target of Rp947.

Two further points of conservatism and one of aggression, stated plainly. Conservative: we deduct minority interests at book value of IDR745.6bn. The minorities earned IDR31.2bn in FY2025, so capitalising that profit share at our own-history P/E of 6.4x would deduct only about a quarter as much and add roughly two hundred rupiah a share to every method — about a fifth of the target. We do not take it. The minority sits in the property vehicle, whose investment property is already carried at fair value, and in the manufacturing joint venture, whose returns are the weakest in the group; a buyer of the whole company would negotiate against the subsidiaries' own value rather than a capitalised profit share struck in a trough year; and the DCF already values those cash flows at their own growth. Book is the LK figure and the right anchor, but the sensitivity is real and it runs in our favour [S3][S5].

Aggressive: the terminal value is 47.2% of enterprise value and it implies an exit EV/EBITDA of just under eight times FY2035E EBITDA, against the own-history 6.7x the cross-check uses — about a fifth more, which is multiple expansion whatever arithmetic produces it. We disclose it rather than bury it, and we test it. Holding the exit multiple at the own-history figure cuts the terminal value by about a sixth; because that value is discounted more than eight years at 11.7%, the cash-flow value falls by around six per cent, to roughly three-quarters above the price. The rating does not depend on the expansion. What justifies the Gordon terminal value is that terminal growth of 3.5% is below nominal GDP and the implied conversion from terminal EBITDA to free cash flow is around two thirds, which is normal for a distributor whose maintenance capex sits below depreciation [deck][S3].

Capital return is the other way to look at the financial assets. The IDR182.7bn bond portfolio and IDR100.0bn of CLI securities are carried at cost in our bridge and are worth their face value to a buyer; together they are about a hundred rupiah a share, a sixth of the price, and a buy-back at today's level would retire a similar share of the equity [S5]. They earn roughly seven per cent, close to the cost of equity, so holding them neither creates nor destroys much value while they sit there. Our target already gives them full credit at book, so a special dividend would not lift the target — it would accelerate cash the valuation already counts, and it would put a floor under the dividend if trading deteriorates. The option matters for the return, not for the value.

What the price implies. At Rp590 the market is capitalising the company at 7.8x our FY2026E earnings and 6.0x our FY2027E EBITDA, with a dividend yield of 11.9%. Running the cash-flow model backwards, the price is consistent with free cash flow shrinking at -5.7% a year in perpetuity, which would mean revenue falling at roughly that rate while margins held. We do not think that is the most probable path: it requires the company to lose volume every year for a decade without losing margin, which is not what a distributor with an exclusive agency and a national network looks like. But it is what an investor buying at this price is being paid to accept, and it is why the dividend yield, not the growth, is the main component of the return.

The first risk is the agency, and it now carries explicit probability weight rather than a sentence. The Sole Agent Agreement with PT Surya Toto Indonesia runs to 31 December 2026 and may be extended by consultation [S3]. Our base case assumes renewal on current terms and gets 45% of the mass. The bear case, at 30%, is renewal on terms that transfer roughly a point and a half of gross margin to the manufacturer and shorten the payment terms; inside that weight we carry a ten-to-fifteen per cent chance of outright non-renewal. For that tail the anchor is the balance sheet, not the cash-flow model: parent book equity of IDR1,767.7bn at 30 September 2026, against a market value of IDR1,593.0bn and with the IDR259.7bn of cash and IDR182.7bn of bonds recoverable ahead of the operating business [S5]. A non-renewal is therefore a poor outcome but not a zero, which is why it belongs inside the bear weight rather than outside the distribution. Likelihood: low but not negligible, and the manufacturer would have to replace a national network while sharing in the profits of the manufacturing and property joint ventures. This is still the risk that governs position size [S3].

The second risk is demand. Primary residential property sales are contracting at 8.4% year on year and prices are barely moving [S8]. If that persists, dealers destock, projects defer and the company discounts to keep volume, which is precisely the mechanism that took gross margin from 29.5% to 28.1% in the first nine months of 2026 [S6][S3]. Likelihood: high that demand stays weak for another year. Impact: moderate, because the company has shown it can hold a margin above the mid-twenties in a down year.

The third risk is cost. The company buys imported product in foreign currency and the rupiah is weak, with the deck's average rate at 17,570 for FY2026E [deck]. The imported lines are the most price-sensitive to the exchange rate, and a further depreciation would either compress margin or push customers toward local product; imported sanitary ware sales already fell fastest in the first nine months of 2026 [S6]. Likelihood: medium. Impact: low to moderate, because imports are the smaller part of the mix.

The fourth risk is competitive. Chinese and other imported brands are available at lower price points and can be bought directly by large dealers, and the company's own imported portfolio competes with the local TOTO range it distributes. Promotion spend rose in 2026 to defend share [S6]; if that becomes structural, the operating-expense ratio stays high and the margin recovery in our forecast does not arrive.

The fifth is governance and related parties, and it has a cash dimension that the first version of this report recorded but did not use. The company buys from an affiliate in which it also holds a joint-venture stake, and trade payables of IDR455.7bn at 30 September 2026 — about a fifth of annual cost of sales — are the principal's money financing the agent's balance sheet [S5]. That payable is what made the 2026 working-capital release so large: if the renewal shortens terms to, say, half of today's, the release reverses as a cash outflow of the order of two hundred and thirty billion rupiah, roughly two thirds of a year's EBITDA, and the FY2026E cash flow that funds the dividend would not recur [S5][S6]. It is a renewal lever, not an operating cost, which is why we carry it in the bear narrative rather than in the base-case margin. Control sits with a family that also appoints the board [S3]. We have found no evidence of abusive transfer pricing, no pledged controlling shares and no special-monitoring status disclosed in the annual report [S3], but the structure means minority holders depend on the terms of a contract negotiated between related parties. Likelihood of a value-destroying related-party transaction: low. Impact: moderate, because the cash pile is the obvious target.

The sixth is liquidity and capital allocation. Free float is 34.8% with average daily value traded of IDR563.8m — a few hundredths of a per cent of market capitalisation, and about a tenth of one per cent of the free float [S0]. The discount in our target is not a judgement plucked from the air: the house limits table assigns a ten per cent haircut to any name trading below two billion rupiah a day, and SPTO sits well inside that band. Deriving it from days to liquidate gives a similar answer and shows why it is not generous: a position equal to a tenth of the free float would take around a hundred sessions to exit at the full three-month average daily value, and no fund trades at a full day's volume. A holder cannot exit a large position quickly, and the discount is a floor rather than a fine calibration. The company holds cash and bonds well in excess of its operating needs; a value-accretive use of that cash would be positive, an unrelated acquisition would be negative, and in the meantime the dividend is the return [S5].

Our three scenarios share the same drivers, shocked in mirrored amounts. The base case, which now carries 45% of the mass, assumes the agency is renewed on current terms, growth of 5.0% in FY2027E and 5.0% in FY2028E, gross margin recovering to 28.6% and the cash dividend held; it is worth Rp1,031. The bear case, at 30%, assumes growth lower by a fixed amount in every year, gross margin lower by a further two and a half points — the mix effect the company has already reported plus the margin it would concede at renewal — and operating costs higher as promotion persists, with payment terms shortened; it is worth Rp684, still above the market price because the dividend and the net cash position do most of the work at this valuation. The bull case, at 25%, assumes the agency is renewed early on current or better terms, the housing programme lifts the project channel and the margin recovers to the FY2024 level on a larger revenue base; it is worth Rp1,533. The shocks are symmetric by construction, so the spread reflects the operating leverage in the model rather than a thumb on the scale [S3][S6].

Signposts that would change our view, in order of importance: any announcement on the agency before the end of 2026, and its terms; the FY2026 gross margin and operating-expense ratio; the split between dealer and project sales in the FY2026 accounts; the pace of housing-programme deliveries [S7]; and the company's use of its financial investments. A renewal announcement would remove the dominant risk and, in our view, close part of the discount to our target; a failure to renew would make the target irrelevant.

Ownership is concentrated and family-based. Two holding companies, PT Multifortuna Asindo and PT Surya Paramitra Abadi, hold the controlling block and the public holds the remainder [S3]; the data pack measures insider ownership at 65.0% and free float at 34.8% [S0]. The board is drawn from the same family: Tjahjono Alim is President Commissioner, Usman Andy Vice President Commissioner and Willianto Alim President Director, with Goh Poh Heng as the independent commissioner [S3]. A single independent commissioner alongside family executives is the minimum the rules require and not a strong check; it is typical of Indonesian family-controlled mid-caps and it is a reason to insist on the dividend as the main channel by which minority holders get value.

Related-party dealings are large in one direction and negligible in the other. The company's trade payables are almost entirely to PT Surya Toto Indonesia, at IDR455.7bn of the total at 30 September 2026 [S5], reflecting the purchase of TOTO product from the affiliate; related-party receivables are negligible [S5]. The trademark licence is a second related-party flow: SPN pays Toto Limited in Japan a fee of 2.0% of its net sales, a contract that runs to 31 October 2031 [S3]. Both arrangements are disclosed, priced by contract and consistent with the way the group is structured, but they mean that a meaningful share of the economics is set between related parties rather than in the market.

Audit and disclosure are adequate. The FY2025 accounts were audited by KAP Teramihardja, Pradhono & Chandra with an unqualified opinion [S3], the annual report is produced in both Indonesian and English, and the quarterly report we use for the September 2026 balance sheet is detailed enough to reconcile cash, investments and minority equity [S5]. We have not found a restatement, a qualification or a change of auditor in the periods we have read.

The dividend record is the best governance fact about the company. DPS was Rp50 in FY2022, Rp60 in FY2023, Rp70 in FY2024 and Rp70 in FY2025, paid as an interim and a final each year, and the board held the cash dividend flat through the FY2025 profit decline rather than cut it [S3][S4]; the FY2025 total was IDR189.0bn, most of parent profit. That record is why our forecast holds the dividend at the FY2025 level instead of scaling it to a trough payout ratio. A controlling family that pays out cash rather than reinvesting it in unrelated ventures is, on the evidence of the last four years, treating minorities reasonably.

Structure flags, classified. Optic-class: family control with a single independent commissioner; a related-party supply contract and a related-party trademark royalty; a free float that limits liquidity. None of these is manipulation-class. We have found no pledge of controlling shares, no going-concern or late-filing notation, no special-monitoring board status, no discounted placement to affiliates and no rights issue in the periods covered by the annual report [S3]. The absence of a disclosure is not proof of absence, and the balance-sheet date we rely on is 30 September 2026; we searched the 9M26 report and the FY2025 annual report for events after the balance-sheet date and found no sale, acquisition, litigation or corporate action beyond the dividend already described [S3][S5].

ESG exposures are those of a ceramics and distribution business. Manufacturing is energy-intensive, so the cost of gas and electricity at the Surabaya plant is both an emissions issue and a margin issue; water use and kiln emissions are the operational footprint; and the property joint venture carries land held under building-use rights with finite terms [S3]. On the social side the company employs a few hundred permanent staff and a larger contracted workforce, and its distribution network extends to small dealers across the outer islands, which is a genuine livelihood footprint. Governance, as set out above, is the weakest of the three. We would want to see a second independent commissioner and a related-party transaction policy with pricing benchmarks before treating governance as a strength.

The calendar is dominated by one date. The Sole Agent Agreement expires on 31 December 2026 and may be extended by consultation between the parties [S3]; an announcement before or shortly after that date is the single event that would re-rate or de-rate the shares. We expect renewal, on the basis that the manufacturer has no Indonesian distribution network of its own and shares in the profits of the manufacturing and property joint ventures, but we do not assume the terms are unchanged.

After that, the reporting calendar. The FY2026 results, expected in the first quarter of 2027 on the recent cadence [S5], will show whether the margin compression of the first nine months of 2026 was a promotion cycle or a new normal. The annual meeting and the final dividend follow in mid-2027, the second half of the payout the company has split since 2022 [S4]. Each quarterly report gives us the cash and investment balances, which are large enough relative to the market value to matter on their own.

The industry calendar gives us the demand read. Bank Indonesia publishes its residential property survey each quarter, and the third-quarter 2026 edition showed sales contracting 8.4% and prices up 0.6% [S8]. The housing programme reports delivery periodically, with 324,213 units reached by mid-June 2026 [S7]. We watch both because they drive the project channel, which is where the company has historically grown when retail was weak [S4].

The KPIs we monitor between updates: the split between local and imported product sales, because the imported lines carry the margin and the currency risk [S6]; the split between dealer, distributor and project sales, because it tells us which channel is carrying the volume [S4][S6]; gross margin and the operating-expense ratio, which together determine whether our FY2027E recovery is plausible; operating cash flow against net profit, and inventory against sales, because the 2026 cash flow was flattered by a working-capital release [S5]; the related-party trade payable balance, as a proxy for how the affiliate relationship is being run [S5]; and any change in the dividend, which would signal a change in the board's view of the future.

What would make us wrong, in one sentence each. If the agency is renewed on terms that shift several points of gross margin to the manufacturer, our base case is too high and the bear case becomes the base [S3]. If Indonesian property sales keep contracting and the company defends volume with price, the margin recovery does not arrive and the earnings multiple is the right way to value it [S8]. If the company deploys its cash and investments into an unrelated acquisition, the balance-sheet support for the valuation weakens [S5]. And if the rupiah weakens sharply, the imported portfolio becomes a cost problem rather than a margin source [S6]. None of these is our central expectation; all of them are visible in the data we monitor, which is what makes the position testable.

S7.title: Antara: 3 Juta Rumah 324,213 units to Jun 2026

S8.title: Antara: BI residential property survey Q3 2026

bear.narrative: Indonesian consumption stays weak, retail dealer sales keep falling, and the TOTO agency is renewed on tighter terms that transfer a little over a point of gross margin to the principal, with related-party payment terms shortened at the same time; imported Chinese brands take premium share, gross margin stays near 9M26 levels and promotion costs do not lapse. The 30% weight includes a 10-15% chance of outright non-renewal, for which the floor is the balance sheet rather than the cash-flow model.

bull.narrative: The agency is renewed early, the housing programme and project pipeline lift volumes, and the fittings push plus a normalisation of promotion spend restore FY2024 margins on a larger revenue base.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E +0.6%: 9M26 sales were +1.9% yoy with 3Q26 down 1.6%, dealers +1.8% but the project channel -3.1% and imported sanitary ware -15.7%; Q4 2025 was a strong base, so we hold sales roughly flat for the year rather than extrapolate the nine-month gain [S6][S4]. FY2027-28 +5.0%: the government housing programme (324,213 units delivered to mid-June 2026) is the swing for the project channel, which grew 3.7% in FY2025 but fell 3.1% in 9M26 [S7][S4][S6], with dealer/distributor demand recovering only as consumption does while primary property sales are still contracting [S8]. The two 5.0% years sit on a flat FY2026E, so the three-year FY2026-28 compound is 3.5% - exactly the company's FY2022-25 revenue CAGR on the pack - and FY2024 already showed an 11.9% recovery year, so this is a return to trend, not above it. Then fade to 4.0% and a 3.5% terminal rate, below long-run IDR nominal GDP.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 28.2%: 9M26 actual 28.1% vs 29.9% a year earlier, the compression driven by mix (imported brands -15.7%) and discounting [S6]. FY2027E 28.4% and FY2028E 28.6% as the mix normalises; 28.6% long run sits below the FY2024-FY2025 average (28.9%/29.5%) because imported premium lines are losing share and competition is promoting [S3][S4].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 18.0%: 9M26 operating expenses were 18.1% of sales (Rp369.4bn) versus 16.8% in FY2025, with the company citing higher professional and promotion fees and event costs [S6][S5]. We hold most of that step-up: 17.5% in FY2027 and 17.2% long run, above the FY2025 actual, because a weaker category needs promotion to defend TOTO share [S3][S4].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 PPE depreciation was Rp65.5bn (2.36% of revenue) per note 14, restated here because the data pack prints Rp30.6bn [S3]. Held at 2.35% in line with the stable asset base and maintenance capex at 2.5% of sales; lease depreciation (Rp9.5bn) is excluded to match the company's own EBITDA definition [S6].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was Rp60.7bn (2.2% of revenue) after the Rp123.1bn FY2024 spend that completed the second production line and showroom work [S3]. We use 2.5% - maintenance of warehouses, showrooms and the SPN plant plus modest IT - not the 3.4% three-year average inflated by 2024.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Average FY2022-FY2024 was 15.4% of revenue; FY2025 jumped to 23% on an inventory build that reversed in 2026 (inventory Rp677.8bn at December 2025 to Rp619.1bn at September 2026, OCF Rp478.4bn in 9M26) [S3][S5]. We use 18.3%, the three-year average the engine computed, as the steady state rather than the FY2025 peak.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax was Rp63.9bn on Rp365.9bn PBT, a 17.4% effective rate; FY2024 was 16.7% [S3]. We use 17.5%, consistent with the statutory 22% less the small-business and interest allowances the accounts show, and leave it flat.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest expense Rp18.3bn on opening debt of Rp274.7bn = 6.7%; 9M26 bank interest paid Rp5.6bn on a shrinking loan book. Use 6.5%.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 9M26 interest received Rp11.6bn plus bond interest Rp8.5bn on cash and a Rp182.7bn bond portfolio; 7.0% on opening cash is consistent.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The short-term bank loan (Rp71.0bn at December 2025) was fully repaid by September 2026 and long-term loans fell Rp9.1bn in 9M26 [S5]; we model Rp20bn of net repayment in FY2026 and flat debt afterwards, with the cash balance funding capex and dividends.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2025 other income of Rp13.1bn was largely interest income plus a Rp6.0bn fair-value loss on investment property; interest income is modelled separately, so we carry zero rather than capitalise a one-off or the property revaluation swing [S3].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: NCI took Rp31.2bn of FY2025 net profit of Rp302.1bn = 10.3%, below its 30% share of equity because the minority sits in the low-return property (SGP, 50%) and manufacturing (SPN, 49%) subsidiaries [S3]. Held at 10.3% - book NCI of Rp745.6bn is deducted in the valuation bridge.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was Rp189bn, Rp70 per share, 62.6% of net profit and 69.8% of profit attributable to the parent; FY2024 was 60% and FY2023 49%, and the board held DPS at Rp70 through the FY2025 profit decline [S4][S3]. We therefore hold the cash dividend at Rp70 in FY2026E, FY2027E and FY2028E - a 92%, 80% and 72% payout as parent profit recovers from the 9M26 trough - and return to the 70% payout from FY2029E. The balance sheet supports it: at 30 Sep 2026 the company held Rp259.7bn of cash and Rp282.7bn of financial investments against Rp179.9bn of gross debt [S5]. A cut to the 70% payout on FY2026E profit, which is what the red team objected to, would be a cut with no source in the board's record.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: 2,700,000,000 shares in issue since the 2018 IPO; no rights issue or buyback announced [S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 3.5%, at the low end of long-run IDR nominal GDP (5.3% real plus ~3% inflation) and below the space's structural growth, because a discretionary building-products distributor whose distribution agreement must be renewed every decade should not carry a GDP-plus terminal rate.

challenges.challenge: The bridge counts the Rp182.7bn bond portfolio twice. methods.dcf adds investments 182.695 (fact F29, S5 p.4) AND the assumptions bridge item 282.695, which is bonds 182.695 plus CLI 100.0 from the same balance sheet, giving equity 3,148.8 instead of 2,966.1. That overstates the DCF by Rp67.7/share (1,166 to 1,099), the EV/EBITDA leg by the same, and the target by about 6% (roughly Rp1,018 to Rp965). The stated net debt of -58.9 also does not reconcile with S5 (cash 259.7 less bank loans 95.7 less leases 84.0 gives net cash 79.9).
challenges.answer: Bridge fixed. The engine already adds the Rp182.7bn bond portfolio as bs_investments (F29), so the assumptions bridge now carries only the Rp100.0bn CLI securities (new fact F58) plus the Rp20.9bn of gross debt repaid between the 30 June pack balance sheet and the 30 Sep LK. Net debt is itemised in 4. Valuation: cash 259.7 less bank loans 95.7 less leases 84.0 less consumer financing 0.2 gives net cash 79.9. Every scenario and the target are restated; the duplicate overstated equity by Rp67.7 per share.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 concedes the terminal value implies an exit multiple above today's but never states it: TV 4,355.0 over FY2035E EBITDA 547.1 is 7.96x against 6.69x on FY2026E, a 19% expansion. Holding today's 6.69x, TV is 3,660 and the DCF falls to about Rp910, below the Rp1,018 target. The house multiple-survival test is therefore failed in substance, not just disclosed.
challenges.answer: The exit multiple is now stated: the terminal value implies just under eight times FY2035E EBITDA against the 6.7x own-history multiple. Holding 6.7x at exit cuts the terminal value by about a sixth and the cash-flow value by around six per cent, still roughly three-quarters above the price, so the rating does not rest on expansion. Terminal growth of 3.5% and an EBITDA-to-FCFF conversion around two thirds are the justification.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 says operating cash flow exceeded net profit in every year we can read. S3 p.94 shows FY2025 net cash from operations of Rp154.1bn against net profit of Rp302.1bn, down Rp288.5bn from Rp442.6bn in FY2024; the accrual gap is Rp148bn, about 4.5% of total assets, the worst of the two years shown. The EARNINGS_QUALITY accruals and cash-conversion screens are missing and the inventory build explains only part of the outflow.
challenges.answer: Section 3 corrected: FY2025 CFO was Rp154.1bn against net profit of Rp302.1bn (new fact F59), after FY2024 CFO of Rp442.6bn (F60). The accrual ratio runs negative in FY2024, about 4 per cent of average assets in FY2025 and strongly negative in 9M26 as inventory released; classified optics-class with the working-capital bridge and the affiliate payable. The old claim that cash flow exceeded profit every year is gone.

challenges.challenge: The bear narrative says the TOTO agency is renewed only on tighter terms, but its shocks are generic mirrors of the bull (-3pp revenue growth, -1.5pp gross margin, +1pp opex) and no scenario carries any probability of non-renewal or of a royalty or margin transfer to the principal. The risk the report itself says governs position size is therefore absent from the probability-weighted Rp1,131.
challenges.answer: Bear raised to 30% and base to 45%. The bear narrative now carries the renewal margin transfer, shortened payables and a stated 10-15% chance of non-renewal, and the gross-margin shock deepens to -2.5pp (mirrored +2.5pp in the bull). The non-renewal floor is parent book equity of Rp1,767.7bn against a Rp1,593bn market value, with cash and bonds recoverable first.

challenges.challenge: The base case cuts DPS 24% to Rp53 in FY2026E by holding the 70% payout on a lower profit, although the company lifted DPS from Rp60 to Rp70 through the FY2025 profit decline, holds Rp259.7bn cash plus Rp282.7bn investments against Rp95.7bn of bank loans [S5], and a flat Rp70 would be a 92% payout on FY2026E parent profit. No source says the board would cut, and the next-12m dividend drives the 81.5% expected return.
challenges.answer: DPS is held at Rp70 in FY2026E-28E instead of cut: payout 92.5%, 79.6% and 72.1%, back to 70% from FY2029E. Sourced to the board holding Rp70 flat through the FY2025 profit decline and to Rp259.7bn of cash plus Rp282.7bn of investments. The next-12m dividend is now Rp70 and the total return is unchanged at 72.4% because the target is struck ex-dividend.

challenges.challenge: Minorities are deducted at book Rp745.6bn, an implied 4.2% return on the Rp31.2bn they earned in FY2025, while the report says the minority sits in low-return property and manufacturing. Capitalising the 10.3% profit share at 6.4x gives roughly Rp135bn, so the deduction is some Rp610bn, or Rp226 per share, 22% of the target. The report calls this conservative but never quantifies it.
challenges.answer: The minority alternative is now quantified: capitalising the 10.3% profit share at the 6.4x P/E would deduct about a quarter as much and add roughly Rp200 a share, about a fifth of the target. We hold book because the property vehicle is already carried at fair value and the manufacturing JV is the weakest asset in the group; the swing is disclosed as running in our favour rather than asserted as conservative.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue of 2,796.0 implies Q4 sales of 754.8, down 2.8% yoy, and Q4 EBITDA of 99.4, down 25.2% from 132.9, while 9M26 EBITDA was down 11.9% and dealers were up 1.8% and distributors up 1.2% [S6]. The strong-base argument explains flat revenue, not a 25% EBITDA drop, and nothing sources the acceleration.
challenges.answer: Q4 walk added: nine-month EBITDA of Rp251.5bn against the FY2026E line implies a Q4 margin above the 9M actual of 12.3%, against a Q4 2025 base several points above its own nine-month average, which is the whole source of the 25% decline. No acceleration is assumed.

challenges.challenge: FY2027E and FY2028E revenue growth of 5.0% each is the largest driver after the discount rate, yet it sits against BI primary residential sales contracting 8.4% with prices up 0.6% [S8] and is sourced only to the 324,213-unit housing programme [S7]. There is no order book, dealer-count target or segment guidance to support a return to growth 4.7pp above the FY2025 actual.
challenges.answer: The 5% is tied to two sourced anchors: the housing programme with 324,213 units delivered is the project-channel driver, and on a flat FY2026E base the FY2026-28 compound is 3.5%, equal to the company FY2022-25 revenue CAGR, so no year is forecast above trend. Basis and section 3 updated. We did not deflate below the trend rate because the BI -8.4% series is a value measure while programme units are the volume support.

challenges.challenge: The WACC of 11.67% uses D/E of 12.6% and pre-tax cost of debt of 9.45% although the company is in net cash (about Rp79.9bn at 30 Sep 2026) and the model's own cost_of_debt input is 6.5%; a net-cash WACC equals COE at 12.2%, which cuts the DCF by roughly 4-5%. Separately, both multiple cross-checks apply own-history multiples to FY2025A earnings and EBITDA, where LTM parent profit is 246.3 not 270.9 and FY2026E EBITDA is 25% lower, so the stated -44.8% and -18.5% gaps understate the divergence.
challenges.answer: The net-cash rebuild does not cut the DCF by 4-5%: setting gearing to zero unlevers the beta from 0.88 to 0.80, giving COE 11.7% and, with no debt to weight, WACC 11.7%, about two basis points above the 11.67% used, because the relevered beta adds less than cheap debt saves. Using the 6.5% effective cost of debt would lower WACC about a quarter point. The cross-check point was accepted: both now state that they use restated FY2025A rather than LTM and that a rolling base would widen both gaps.

challenges.challenge: The Rp455.7bn of related-party trade payables to PT Surya Toto Indonesia equals about 23% of annual COGS and is what funds the working-capital position the FY2026E cash flow depends on. If the principal tightens payment terms at renewal, or the agency lapses, the release reverses; the report records the payable but never treats it as a renewal lever or a liquidity risk.
challenges.answer: Quantified: the Rp455.7bn affiliate payable is about a fifth of cost of sales; halving payment terms reverses the 9M26 working-capital release as a cash outflow of the order of Rp230bn, about two thirds of a year of EBITDA. It is carried in the bear narrative as a renewal lever and in section 5 as a liquidity risk.

challenges.challenge: The CLI Rp100bn and bond Rp182.7bn portfolios, plus the revalued SGP property, are valued at cost with no sum-of-parts or capital-return sensitivity, even though the family has raised DPS every year since FY2022 and the investments earn about 7%, near the cost of equity. A special dividend or buyback is not considered anywhere.
challenges.answer: Capital-return sensitivity added: the bond and CLI portfolios are worth about Rp105 a share, a sixth of the price, and a buy-back at today levels would retire a similar share of the equity. They earn about 7%, near the cost of equity, so distributing them accelerates cash the target already counts rather than adding value, but it floors the dividend.

signoff.notes: Base is calibrated to the 9M2026 actuals (EBITDA margin 12.3%, revenue flat on a +1.9% nine-month base) rather than a haircut, the 5% FY2027-28 recovery is tied to the housing programme and the FY2022-25 CAGR, and the 10% liquidity discount is mechanical from the turnover band. The FATAL double-count in the bridge is fixed, the TOTO agency renewal now carries 30% of the weight with a 10-15% non-renewal tail inside it, and the payout drift is the cash DPS held at Rp70 rather than a cut. One inconsistency for the desk, not a defect in this report: minorities are deducted at book Rp745.6bn here while TOTO marks the same SGP/SPN joint ventures at 12x earnings (Rp374bn) in its own bridge; the report quantifies the alternative at about Rp200 a share. Align the pair at the next review. Approve.

bias.note: Base-case drivers sit at or below the last actual and at the board own behaviour, each sourced: FY2028E gross margin 28.6% vs 29.5% FY2025A and 28.9% FY2024 on the imported-mix decline [S6]; long-run opex 17.2% vs 16.8% FY2025A; terminal g 3.5% vs ~8.6% nominal GDP and the 3.5% revenue CAGR since FY2025A; DPS held flat at Rp70; minorities at book Rp745.6bn. Scenarios are mirrored (+/-3pp growth, +/-2.5pp GM, -/+1pp opex), base 45% >= 40%. No unsourced haircut or uplift found in either direction.

findings.finding: The recorded extreme_call justification misstates the model own outputs in three places: it calls cash + Rp182.7bn bonds + Rp100.0bn CLI 23% of the market capitalisation when Rp542.4bn is 34.0% of the Rp1,593bn market cap (22.8% only if netted against Rp179.9bn gross debt); it puts the FY2026E dividend yield near nine per cent when s4 and the multiples table show 11.9% (Rp70 over Rp590); and it says the price implies revenue falling about 10% a year when the reverse DCF returns -5.7% (the -0.107 is the adjustment applied to a 5.0% base, not the implied rate). The published report text is correct on all three; only the record is wrong.

The report headline quotes the engine 6.0x FY2027E EV/EBITDA while the extreme_call justification quotes 5.8x. The gap is the EV convention: the engine uses FY2026E forecast net debt of Rp14.6bn, the justification uses the Rp79.9bn September net cash. Both are defensible but the reader should see one number.

The DCF stub starts at the pack balance-sheet date (30 June 2026, FY2026 fraction 0.504) while net debt uses 30 September 2026 cash. About three months of FY2026E FCFF (~Rp90bn, ~Rp34 per share, 3.0% of the DCF) is counted on top of cash that already contains it; the target effect is ~2% (Rp20), so the rating does not turn on it.

Interest income is modelled as 7% of opening cash only (Rp8.1bn in FY2026E) although the company holds Rp259.7bn cash, Rp182.7bn bonds and Rp100.0bn CLI earning ~7%. Parent profit is understated by roughly Rp25-30bn pre-tax (~Rp9-10 per share) in FY2026-27. Direction is conservative and FCFF is unaffected (interest sits below EBIT and the portfolios are added at face), so the DCF value is right but the P/E cross-check and dividend cover read low.

flags.message: a.payout moves -22.5pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The payout percentage falls from 92.5% in FY2026E to 70% from FY2029E because we hold the cash dividend at Rp70 a share while parent profit recovers; the dividend itself does not fall in any year of the forecast. That is the board's own behaviour: DPS was held at Rp70 in FY2025 through a 4.7% revenue decline [S4][S3], and Rp259.7bn of cash plus Rp282.7bn of financial investments against Rp179.9bn of gross debt fund it [S5]. The payout returns to the FY2025 level of 70% as earnings normalise, which is why the ratio drifts rather than the dividend.

The base case assumes the sole-agent agreement is renewed.
